top.title: Create the social accounts (Mastodon, Bluesky) and hand them to Aros - chamber#1, open 8 days 10 hours and the oldest item ever to sit on this desk. The issue carries the measured platform rules as of 2026-07-26 12:11 UTC, and they changed the recommendation: Bluesky has no bot-labelling convention at all (neither its Community Guidelines of 2025-09-19 nor its ToS of 2025-08-14 mention bots, automation or AI content), and on Mastodon the binding rules are per-server - mastodon.social and mstdn.social, the two obvious open-registration servers, both exclude an account like this one outright. infosec.exchange or techhub.social instead, with a paste-ready sign-up reason in the comment. This is the phase exit: every bet in the strategy needs an audience and there is none

others.title: Create a GitHub account for Aros, invite it to the org, and mint its token with contents + issues + pull-requests + repo-metadata scope - one action closes chamber#3 (he files issues from your account, which guardrail 8 forbids, and it is the standing violation on this list) and chamber#6 (no pull requests, no topics, no descriptions, no security settings). Open 7 days 6 hours and 7 days 4 hours. This page is the argument in miniature: the issue count on it has to be produced by matching a disclosure sentence in issue prose, because GitHub's own authorship metadata cannot separate his 38 issues from your 7

retinue#1, open 7 days 14 hours - the projects card returns no rows because web-gateway's query and md2ttl.py disagree on namespace, predicate and actor URI shape. It is also why the framework's only proactivity feature has never fired in any deployment: agent-self-review ships enabled at 86400 s, so it runs daily everywhere, and its whole gate is one SPARQL query returning zero rows. The actor join fails on its own - discover-agents.py emits urn:retinue:actor:aros with a colon while both public converters build actor-aros with a hyphen, and the hyphen form is what docs/triple-stores.md and qlever-dir's example tell people to write. Decide which shape is canonical; the fix is one line on whichever side you choose

Enable private vulnerability reporting on the four public repos - chamber#5, open 7 days 5 hours, re-checked 2026-07-27 08:12 UTC and still false on all four. The SECURITY.md on the unmerged chamber branch gives a reporting path that does not depend on it, which fixes the worst half; the Code of Conduct's enforcement link still routes to the disabled feature. Verify your own fix with: gh api /repos/retinue-os/<repo>/private-vulnerability-reporting - it answers without admin scope. A comment on the issue from 2026-07-26 15:21 UTC records why this one matters more than its age suggests: the dashboard substitutes for the missing reporting path, and nine agent-initiated threads on it are unread

Nine threads are waiting on your dashboard, the oldest since 2026-07-19 20:25 UTC (7 days 11 hours), all nine unread and none replied to, re-measured 2026-07-27 08:15 UTC. The card lists five, so four are reachable only through All conversations. Their contents are deliberately not described here or on any other public surface; each thread carries what to do, what was already prepared, and what happens if you do nothing. The three live ones are 2026-07-19 21:33 UTC (the privacy decision - whether to purge this chamber repo's history of text redacted on 2026-07-20; doing nothing leaves the redaction standing and degrades nothing), 2026-07-25 21:21 UTC and 2026-07-26 13:26 UTC. Read the newest two before the oldest. Since 2026-07-26 only one agent thread stays open at a time, so new findings append to the newest rather than adding a badge

Merge (or reject) the branch claude/aros-issues-triage-goei5k on this chamber repo - it replaces the GUARDRAILS.md section 3 CI row (chamber#7, open 7 days 3 hours) and adds SECURITY.md. Still unmerged with no pull request; this repository has never had one. One change before merging: the row it adopts is Aros's own earlier wording, and its clause about the gateway's security-critical paths being untested is false as written - path traversal and SPARQL-injection containment are exercised in four test files. The corrected sentence ("endpoint authorization is untested by construction: no test constructs the gateway's request handler") is in a comment on chamber#7 from 2026-07-25 16:40 UTC

Fix or triage the two security issues you filed - retinue#15 (credentials inherited by agent subsessions; this session carries a repo-write token, a billable API key, a gateway master key and a database password) and retinue#19 (agent can self-approve a verify-policy send). Open 5 days 23 hours and 5 days 12 hours. Both unfixed, so the affected claims stay withdrawn from positioning.md, and the two claim-correction issues below cannot close until they move

Merge the two claim corrections that follow from those - retinue#26 and retinue#27, open 3 days 1 hour and 2 days 18 hours. Between them the false or unscoped sentence appears in nine public places (README, comparison.md, review.md, .env.example, a gateway docstring, an agent-facing skill file). No new prose needed: the correct wording already exists elsewhere in the same repo in both cases

Create retinue-os/.github and set the org and repo descriptions - chamber#4, open 7 days 5 hours. Draft text is paste-ready in writing/org-profile-README.md; three of four public repos still have no description and no repo in the org carries a topic. This is also the discoverability item: an authenticated GitHub search for "retinue" ranked the framework 12th of 50 at 2026-07-26 17:36 UTC, and with 0 stars description is most of what search has to rank on. That reading was deliberately not re-taken this morning - it moves when the descriptions land, not daily. This project's expected date was 2026-07-25 and it arrived unmet

retinue#39, filed 2026-07-27 04:58:33 UTC, is the newest and is two findings in one issue: each of two services assumes the /tmp lifetime the other one has. signal-gateway loses the queue of verify-category outbound messages on the documented update path, silently, after signal-push.py has already reported them queued for approval; qlever-static rebuilds its index from a stale cached decompression on the documented reindex recipe and reports "Index built." The only shipped example configuration is the affected one. Both are one-line fixes in opposite directions - give signal-gateway's /tmp a volume, or stop caching by existence

Three issues from 2026-07-26 are still unseen - retinue#36, #37, #38. #37 first: git-serialize.sh, the shim two agents rely on to not clobber each other, matches "git commit" but not "git -C <repo> commit", and the second form is what the web gateway's own auto-commit uses, so the framework's principal caller of the lock bypasses it. #36: the three push CLIs' --help describes the send policy as a property of the recipient, while the gateways, the tests and four docs key it to the sending identity - and that help text is what an agent reads while deciding whether to claim a send was approved. #38: the two shipped example chamber agents assert a chamber confinement SECURITY.md lists as a known limitation, in the files examples/chambers/README.md calls the canonical authoring reference

Allow GitHub Actions to create pull requests - retinue#4, open 6 days 21 hours and the last item on this desk still under a week; it crosses at 2026-07-27 11:04:39 UTC. check-signal-cli pushes its bump branch and then cannot open the PR, so the automation completes and delivers nothing. Same missing permission as chamber#6, through a different door

Triage the remaining defects in the indexing mechanism the lead story rests on - qlever-dir#8 (blank nodes collide across files; you proposed skolemizing per graph on 2026-07-25 and Aros answered the same day, latest comment 2026-07-26 10:18 UTC) and #10 (a directory created after startup is never watched, which is exactly how the framework's own boot emitters write). #9 in that set is closed - filed 2026-07-23 15:53 UTC, merged 2026-07-25 15:14 UTC, 47 hours - and its fix is verified here against a fixture covering five symlink shapes

retinue#2 needs a decision rather than a merge, and is 7 days 9 hours old. Its branch docs/calibrate-reindex-latency replaces the docs' "~15 s" with "15-20 s for a small file", and that number is stale: re-measured 2026-07-25 in this deployment it is 20-25 s over three trials with no code change, because the chamber grew from 340 KB to 1.4 MB. Merging the branch as pushed would write a fresh wrong number into the framework. The replacement wording, with method and bounds, is in a comment from 2026-07-25 20:36 UTC. The second branch on that issue, docs/link-provenance-piece, is unaffected and still worth merging

retinue#28 is on main rather than on a branch: PR #22 merged 2026-07-25 15:12 UTC with both items unaddressed - docs/triple-stores.md states the _generated indexing as unconditional, and the model slug is not injective. Aros corrected his own suggested fix in the thread; take the corrected one

review.md is stale on tests and CI: recommendation #2 is done and six statements are now false - retinue#3, open 7 days 3 hours. Two items on its edit list are struck as superseded, with replacements in the thread; the counts it proposed have gone stale twice, so reword without counts rather than refreshing them

Nothing new will arrive here before 2026-07-28 04:58 UTC, and that is a rule rather than a lull: one new issue per 24 hours while nothing is inbound and the queue is above 20 open. Five findings are written up in full and waiting, the oldest since 2026-07-25 05:23 UTC; they sit in drafts/ in this chamber, readable now, each stating whether it was filed and where. If you would rather see findings as they are found, say so and the limit goes
